text:
WARDOGS has no fixed class selection at spawn. Each life, a player spends cash at a vendor to build a custom loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1]. Experience is earned on role tracks (Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot) that gate which items can be bought [6]. Gunplay is described by the developer as realistic but tuned for gameplay rather than simulation [1].

The official Steam page confirms the loadout-per-life model, melee, sniping, destructible environments and buildable forward operating bases, but it publishes no weapon list, damage values or ballistic parameters [1]. Specific weapon names, prices and category-to-track mappings in this document come from press and player-reported coverage, much of it from the closed beta, and are labelled as such.

Document confidence is Medium: the structural model is official, but the weapon-level detail rests on secondary, partly pre-release sources, and the official Season 1 patch text could not be retrieved directly (see Open Questions).

## Loadout selection and economy

Loadouts are purchased at a vendor each life. A guide dated 17 Sep 2026 reports that after death a player returns to the vendor and can use "Re-buy Loadout" to rebuild the prior kit, and that repeated deaths can drain cash; it gives no exact cost [6] (player-reported). A level requirement only unlocks the option to buy: a one-time unlock payment is required, after which the item has a normal per-life vendor price (player-reported, Sep 2026 guides) [6].

Example unlock costs reported by that guide, all player-reported [6]:

| Item | Unlock | One-time cost |
|------|--------|---------------|
| PP-19 Vityaz | Medic 4 | one-time payment (amount not stated) |
| Galil | Assault 10 | $35,000 |
| Individual First Aid Kit | Medic 9 | $25,000 |
| Defibrillator | Medic 11 | $50,000 ($1,600 per loadout purchase) |
| Adrenaline Pen | Medic 14 | $25,000 |
| Basic Parachute | n/a | $100 |

The Emergency Resuscitator is reported free and usable once per life for reviving teammates [6]. Small, medium and large tactical vests open additional quick slots [6]. Patch notes say 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables take up more loadout space [3].

## Weapon categories and notable weapons (beta list, not final)

A press table recorded vendor list prices during testing and states they are not confirmed as the shipping economy [5]. Entries below are examples only.

| Category | Examples (beta list price) |
|----------|----------------------------|
| Assault rifles | Bushmaster M17S ($0), AK74 ($1,600), M4 ($2,800), FAL ($6,500) |
| SMGs | AMP-9 ($900), MP5 ($1,500), PP-19 Vityaz ($1,200) |
| Shotguns | MP43 ($400), M500 ($1,200) |
| LMGs | M249 SAW ($3,200), PKM ($4,500) |
| Marksman rifles | SKS ($2,400), SVD ($4,800) |
| Sniper rifles | Mosin Nagant ($4,500), AMR 50 ($8,800) |
| Bow | Compound Bow ($800) |
| Sidearms | M1911 ($300), Deagle ($900) |
| Launchers | RPG-7 ($2,000), MAAWS ($2,600), 9K333 Verba (surface-to-air) |

The same source reports ammo billed separately by caliber (roughly $10 to $250 a box), a 50% vendor discount below WARDOG Level 9, and attachments (optics, foregrips, magazines) unlocked by level rather than purchase [5]. 33 weapons were recorded, with 37 expected at launch [5]. These beta values predate the Season 1 repricing [3], so treat them as stale.

## Roles and progression

Press-reported beta mapping of kills to tracks: Assault XP from assault rifles and sidearms, Medic from SMGs, Support from shotguns, LMGs and launchers, Recon from marksman rifles, sniper rifles and the bow [5]. A later guide lists six tracks including Driver and Pilot, and says each track unlocks weapons, equipment, attachments and vehicles [6]. These disagree on track count (four in the beta list versus six), consistent with changes between beta and launch; the official breakdown was not found.

Season 1 changes (10 Sep 2026, via press) [3]:

- Role-track XP requirements rose sharply in the middle band: level 10 from 25,000 to 35,000, level 15 from 54,750 to 110,000, level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000; levels below 6 unchanged.
- Unlock shifts included Deagle from level 90 to 85, PP-19 50-round drum from level 29 (was 33), and Large Hammer from level 7 to 8.
- Recon scopes repriced: 6-10x MRAD $25,000 to $40,000; 6-10x MOA $30,000 to $45,000.
- Support: Medium Hammer $10,000 to $25,000; Large Hammer $25,000 to $75,000; vendor Forward Operating Base $2,500 to $7,500.
- Air vehicle player-kill XP lowered from 300 to 250.

## Damage and ballistics

No official damage values, armor ratings or ballistic tables were found. The developer states gunplay is tuned for gameplay rather than simulation [1]. Press reports that real bullet drop and travel time are modelled and that weapon weights differ (for example AMR 50 12.5 kg, LMGs 7.5 kg) [5]. Patch 0.1.2 notes that buildable "crit spots" were reworked and a Havoc bug that increased damage from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire was fixed [4]; this indicates locational critical spots exist on buildables, but no further model is documented.

## Gadgets and utility

Officially named: ghillie suit, rocket launchers, forward operating bases [1]. Via patch notes: throwables (grenades, smoke, C4), parachutes, backpacks, flares and hammers [3][4]. Player-reported: smoke grenades, first aid kit, defibrillator, adrenaline pen [6].

text:
WARDOGS runs a persistent cash economy. Every player starts with $10,000, team-play actions earn cash, cash carries from match to match, and each life the player buys a loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1]. The publisher states that cash "determines the risks players can take" and that outcomes are reflected in the account balance, and that in-game cash cannot be bought with real money [3]. As of the Steam Early Access launch the price is £36.99 (Standard) on the UK Steam page, with a £45.99 Supporter Edition [1].

Official sources confirm the broad loop but publish no full price or reward table. Specific price changes come from the Season 1 launch changelog as reproduced by press [4]; the death penalty, per-action rewards and full vehicle costs are described only in community guides and are labelled player-reported here. Verified against the Steam store page and the Steam news feed as of 2026-10-08, latest minor patch 0.1.2 [1][2].

Document confidence is Medium: the core loop is official, but most numbers rest on secondary reproductions and community measurements.

text:
## Earning cash

Official sources say only that teamplay actions reward cash and that an end-of-match bonus exists [1][5]. A community guide lists kills and assists, revives and heals, teammate tips, spotting, ground transport and supply runs, FOB building, holding the Control Zone, Hot Zone actions (reported as paying double) and destroying enemy vehicles as income sources, with no amounts (player-reported) [6]. Patch 0.1.2 reduced rewards for destroying buildables and for depositing outside a FOB zone, and closed vehicle fly-through exploits [2].

## Spending cash

Cash buys the per-life loadout [1]. The Season 1 launch changelog (10 Sep 2026) lists these changes [4]:

| Item | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| Forward Operating Base (vendor) | $2,500 | $7,500 |
| Large Hammer (vendor) | $1,600 | $2,400 |
| Support Large Hammer | $25,000 | $75,000 |
| Career Artillery Tank | $400,000 | $500,000 |
| Pilot Little Bird with miniguns | $25,000 | $50,000 |
| Pilot Z20 Lakota | $50,000 | $35,000 |
| Driver URAL | $50,000 | $35,000 |
| Driver Dune Buggy | $35,000 | $25,000 |
| Driver Kodiak Flatbed | $15,000 | $35,000 |

Other lines in the same changelog cover scope, hammer and crate prices and a rescaled supply-crate purchase curve [4]. Another outlet described the Kodiak Flatbed as a reduction, which conflicts with the figures above; see Open Questions.

Per-spawn vehicle prices (for example $500 for a Bobcat, about $8,000 for the SPH-2, about $18,000 for the Havoc) are community measurements, not an official table, and the source warns they may change (player-reported) [7].

## Death penalty

Official pages say a player buys a loadout each life and that outcomes feed the balance [1][3], but do not state the exact loss on death. Community guides report that if a downed player is not revived the kit bought for that life is lost, the next kit is paid from the same balance, and helicopter crashes can destroy the loadouts of the pilot and passengers (player-reported) [6][7].

## Persistence and seasons

Cash persists between matches [1]. Community guides claim cash and XP reset each season and that leftover cash converts to Gold Bars; this is not confirmed in any official source retrieved (player-reported, see Open Questions) [8].

## Monetization

| Product | Price (Steam, 2026-10-08) |
|---------|---------------------------|
| WARDOGS | £36.99 [1] |
| Supporter Edition | £45.99 [1] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC) | £11.99 [1] |

The launch press release quoted $39.99 USD for Early Access [3].

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter in Steam Early Access since 10 September 2026. Its core mode is the Control Zone: teams contest a randomised 2x2 km zone, the team with the most players inside scores, and the first to 100 points wins [1][3]. Local voice chat is heard across all three teams, and the Steam page describes it as proximity voice chat [1][3].

Progression is cash-based within and across matches, plus a role-track XP system that gates unlocks and resets each season [1][5][9]. The developer's stated 1.0 direction is a wider meta game and long-term systems, more maps, weapons and vehicles, deeper progression, a seasonal meta game and fighter jets [1][3]. Season 02 is announced for 15 October 2026 [7].

Confidence is Medium. The match format, voice chat, cash and Early Access plans rest on the Steam page and the Team17 press release. The role-track detail, hot-zone and tower mechanics, and the October patch contents rest on press and player-reported sources, because the official Steam announcement text could not be read directly in this session.

text:
- Format: up to 100 players in three teams; the Early Access launch set is three maps, each with three variations (verified 2026-10-08) [1][3].
- Objective: a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone; the team with the most players inside earns points; first to 100 wins; a Hot Zone gives double cash [1].
- Voice: local voice chat carries across all three teams, so enemies in earshot can be heard [3].
- Progression: cash carries between matches and every teamplay action pays [1]; XP also accrues to role tracks that gate unlocks (player-reported structure, see Detail) [5][9].
- Seasons: Season 01 ran from launch; Season 02 is announced for 15 Oct 2026 with a reset of cash and XP while Gold Bars and cosmetics persist [7].
- Modes: the Control Zone is the only official mode named at Early Access; community servers can run modified modes, and a Deploy flow steers new players to Infantry mode and low-level community servers as of 0.1.2 [3][4][6].
- 1.0: no date or dated roadmap has been given; Early Access is expected to last around one to two years [1][8].

text:
All statements verified 2026-10-08 against the sources shown.

- Early Access began 10 Sep 2026; the developer describes it as fully playable and representing the core vision, expected to last around 1 to 2 years [1].
- Matches support up to 100 players split across three rival teams [1][3].
- Teams fight for a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone; the team with the most players in the zone earns points and the first to 100 wins [1].
- A Hot Zone offers double cash [1].
- Players start with $10,000 and buy a loadout each life; teamplay actions such as reviving, transporting teammates and holding the objective earn cash; cash carries over between matches [1].
- Local voice chat can be heard across all three teams [3]; the Steam page lists proximity voice chat [1].
- Launch content is three maps, each with three variations, with infantry and vehicle combat [3].
- Patch 0.11 (14 Sep 2026) split the server browser into Official and Community lists and added a 5% end-of-match cash bonus on Community servers for one week [4]. Note the French and German press number versions differently, so version labels vary by outlet [4][6].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) added server-side checks on revives, capped rewards for destroying buildables by construction progress, reduced rewards for depositing pallets outside designated zones, and added a Deploy flow toward Infantry mode and low-level community servers [6].
- The 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes are reported inconsistently: one outlet says no gameplay or balance changes [6], another reports IR rangefinders disabled until Season 02 and a faster CWIS kill on the Havoc [7].
- Season 02 is announced for 15 Oct 2026 via a developer Steam teaser dated 22 Sep 2026, as relayed by a third party [7].

text:
## Match format and objectives

| Element | Fact at Season 01 | Source |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| Players | Up to 100 | [1][3] |
| Teams | 3 | [1][3] |
| Zone | Randomised 2x2 km Control Zone per match | [1] |
| Win condition | First team to 100 points | [1] |
| Scoring basis | Most players in zone earns points | [1] |
| Hot Zone | Double cash | [1] |
| Maps | 3, each with 3 variations | [3] |

Player-reported mechanics (not stated on the Steam page): a tick of roughly one point every 30 seconds; each player in the Hot Zone counts as two for presence; three to five tower capture points inside the Control Zone; completing a code from towers lets a team drag the Hot Zone toward a held tower [10][11]. Sources differ on exact wording, so treat these as player-reported.

## Local cross-team voice chat

The press release says local voice chat is audible across all three teams [3]. The Season 01 changelog as reported by press lists fixes to voice dropping after a failed join, to push-to-talk targeting and re-login recovery, plus a visible communication status [5].

## Progression and unlocks

| Element | Detail | Source |
|---------|--------|--------|
| Starting cash | $10,000 per life loadout budget | [1] |
| Cash earning | Teamplay actions, holding objective | [1] |
| Role tracks | Six tracks reported (Assault or Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot); naming differs between sources | [5][9] |
| Track cap | Level 100 per track and account level to 600, player-reported | [9] |
| Unlock cost | Reaching a level makes an item buyable for a one-time cash fee, player-reported | [9] |
| Season reset | Cash and XP reset; leftover cash converts to Gold Bars; Gold Bars and cosmetics persist | [7] |
| Per-season curve | "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" (quoted from the Season 1 changelog by a third party) | [7] |

Season 01 XP changes reported by press: level 10 rose from 25,000 to 35,000 XP, level 15 from 54,750 to 110,000, level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000, level 50 from 838,000 to 1,000,000; air vehicle kills pay 250 XP, down from 300 [5]. Economy abuse penalties (timed bans with cash and XP reset, permanent bans for XP farming) were reported in the 0.11 notes [4].

## Modes available at Early Access

The only official mode named is the Control Zone [1][3]. Official servers do not run modified game modes, while Community servers can [4]. The 0.1.2 Deploy flow points new players at Infantry mode and low-level community servers [6]. Assessment: a full catalogue of community-server modes could not be verified; confidence Low.

## Planned for 1.0

Developer statements: more maps, weapons and vehicles, deeper progression, a seasonal meta game and fighter jets [1]; continued work toward the wider meta game and long-term systems for 1.0 [3]. A third-party roadmap article additionally lists new objective types, a Black Market and Vault, and Player Skills and Challenges, but does not say which are official [8]. The developer reportedly will not publish a dated roadmap [8].

text:
## Reconciling "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations"

The Steam page says "sandbox" and "maps" with no count [1]. The press release gives the count: three maps with three variations each [2]. These are compatible: "sandbox" describes the build-and-destroy freedom, while the press release counts discrete map assets. Assessment: Medium confidence that this is the intended reading, because neither official source defines either term.

The word "variations" is not defined. A community guide lists about three or four named areas per map (for example Default, Farmland, Lumberyard on Bakurani) that come up from a rotation, with some defined areas never selected [11]. This plausibly matches the "three variations" count but is an inference; no source confirmed sunrise or cloudy variants of the maps. Treat the equivalence as unverified.

## Community-reported map roster (Season 01, player-reported)

| Map | Region label | Described terrain | Relative size | Source |
|-----|--------------|-------------------|---------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Kavkazi | River valley, town, factory district, snow-capped northern mountains | Smallest | [9][10][11] |
| Ozeti | Europe | Wooded river basin, hill town, walled football stadium, church, farmland | About 4x Bakurani | [9][10][11] |
| Zestafona | North America | River bend, warehouse and rail districts, shipping, farmland, forest | About 4x Bakurani | [9][10][11] |

A further "Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari" sniper map and "Saburtulo" appear in one roster but are listed as not confirmed playable or not playable [11]. They are not counted as launch maps.

## Points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Named features | Source |
|-----|----------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, Sunflower complex and church, Lumberyard, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, numbered towers | [10] |
| Ozeti | Stadium complex, hillside churches, Shops, Pool, Industrial, Lumberyard, farms, numbered towers | [10] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, large factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, Offices, Water Towers, farmland | [10] |

One guide counts 171 control zones across the three maps [10]. Another records three or four zone positions per map and three live tower objectives on Zestafona [9]. These counts differ, so no figure is given as fact.

## Size

| Claim | Value | Class | Source |
|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| Control Zone | Randomised 2x2 km inside a larger battlefield | Official | [1] |
| Whole map | 256 km2, fully destructible | Third-party roadmap | [7] |
| Whole world | About 16 km edge to edge | Community | [11] |
| Play circle | 500 m radius (550 m Ozeti) | Community | [11] |

Assessment: 16 km x 16 km equals 256 km2, so the two whole-map figures agree, but both are unofficial (Low confidence). The 500 m radius play-circle claim conflicts with the official 2x2 km zone and is not adopted [1][11].

## Destructibility

Official: a destructible battlefield where rocket launchers destroy apartment blocks [1]; the press release lists destruction as a core pillar alongside construction [2]. No source gives a per-structure destruction model, which terrain can be deformed, or whether damage persists across matches. A third-party piece says terrain as well as buildings can be reshaped [7]; the official sources only mention buildings.

## Weather and time of day

Rain is the only announced weather addition, shown in the Season 02 teaser as heavy rain and storm imagery [3][4][8]. Bulkhead says it is a per-map state fixed for the match [3]. One press piece reports it is unconfirmed whether rain affects visibility or vehicles [4]. No day/night cycle is documented in any source read; a claim of existing sunrise, cloudy and sunny states was seen only in a search summary and is not relied on.

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter developed by BULKHEAD (Derby, UK) and published by Team17 [1][2]. It entered Steam Early Access on 10 September 2026 at a Standard price of GBP 36.99 on the UK Steam page and USD 39.99 in the launch press release [1][2][7]. Console versions are planned for "sometime in 2028" [4][5]. The developers expect Early Access to last about one to two years, with a higher price at full release [1].

Since launch the game has had a launch-day Season 1.0 changelog (10 Sep), Patch 0.11 (14 Sep), Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep) and a security and stability hotfix (2 Oct) [8][9][10]. Season 02 is scheduled for 15 October 2026 but its contents are only partly known [11][12]. Steam shows a "Mostly Positive" review rating [1].

Confidence is Medium. Dates, platforms, price and the developer's roadmap text come from the Steam page and Team17, but patch contents rest on press summaries because Steam news bodies do not render to fetchers, and Season 02 detail comes from secondary or conflicted sources.

## Developer, publisher and platforms

BULKHEAD is a Derby-based studio founded in 2015, previously known for The Turing Test and Battalion 1944; Team17 (part of everplay Group plc) publishes [2]. The Steam page lists BULKHEAD as developer and Team17 as publisher [1]. As of 2026-10-08 the playable platform is PC via Steam, with Windows 10 minimum and Windows 11 recommended [1]; Team17's game page also lists NVIDIA GeForce NOW [3]. Xbox and PlayStation are planned for "sometime in 2028", with Xbox wishlists open on the Xbox Store (11 Sep 2026) [4][5].

## Editions and pricing (checked 2026-10-08)

| Item | Steam price | Source |
|------|-------------|--------|
| WARDOGS (Standard) | GBP 36.99 | [1] |
| Supporter Edition (base game plus Supporter Pack) | GBP 45.99 | [1] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC, sold separately) | GBP 11.99 | [1] |

The launch press release gave USD 39.99 for Early Access [2], and a pre-launch press piece gave "$39.99 / GBP 36.99" together [7]. These are the same Standard edition in different currencies. GBP 45.99 is the Supporter Edition, a separate SKU. The Supporter Pack is cosmetic only, and there is no other in-game monetisation during Early Access; in-game cash, gold bars and status camouflage are not sold [2]. See economy-foundation for in-game cash. The developers say the game is priced lower during Early Access with a higher price at full release; the full price is not disclosed [1][2].

## Reception (checked 2026-10-08)

Steam shows "Mostly Positive": 79% positive among 63,152 English reviews, plus 143 curator reviews [1]. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026, so the rating label has held through the first four weeks while the volume grew [1][5]. No finer-grained trend data was found.

## Developer roadmap statement

The Steam page lists intended work: more maps, weapons, vehicles and gameplay variety; deeper progression and a stronger seasonal meta game; rewards for combat, support and logistics; new vehicle types including fighter jets; expanded weapon categories and extra objective variants; continued balance, performance and stability work [1]. The launch release adds that work continues toward the wider meta game and long-term systems for the 1.0 release [2]. No dated roadmap to 1.0 is published; the only dated item is Season 02 on 15 Oct 2026 [11].

## Community channels

The Steam store page and Steam News hub for app 1867240 are the primary announcement channel [1][13]. Team17's WARDOGS page links Team17's Discord (discord.com/invite/team17), the Team17 X account and a Team17 YouTube channel [3]. A WARDOGS-specific official Discord or X account was not confirmed; see Open Questions.

## Performance and settings changes at launch (Season 1 changelog, 10 Sep 2026) [4]

- DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without a restart; the render target pool is configurable.
- Shadow cache refreshes were reduced (less hitching when taking control of a character); shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores instead of being disabled.
- Dropped items no longer affect navigation.
- Startup reliability improved with clearer early-failure messages and a recovery path; a legacy graphics dependency was removed.
- Crash fixes covered two frame generation paths, network calls scheduled off the game thread, a chatbox tooltip, buildables, and firing a weapon whose owner had left. GPU crash reports include more detail.
- Voice chat recovery after a failed join and under load was improved.
- Netcode: none of the sources read describe tick rate, prediction or lag compensation. This is a gap, not a finding.

## Moderation and anti-cheat systems

- A report tracking system weights reports so repeat and bad-faith reporters have less influence; cheater bans are announced in the server when match termination is off; the "kicked from server" message appears only for real bans [4].
- Patch 0.11 states cash exploits get a timed ban plus a reset of cash and XP; exploit tutorials count as advertising cheats and risk permanent bans; the developer states "We track every server you enter" and joining known XP farming servers for more than a few minutes risks a permanent ban [3].

Source warning: no official server-admin manual from Bulkhead was found. Everything in this section other than the 0.1.2 admin changes comes from unofficial or provider material and is labelled.

**Hosting model.**

- A fan site (self-described as unofficial, checked 2026-09-01) relays an official thread saying server code will not be released for everyone to host, citing performance and security, and that individuals rent from approved hosts [9]. Player-reported.
- A server-tracking site says there is no official developer documentation, that only three approved hosts run servers, and that RCON access depends on the host's panel [11]. Player-reported.
- Consequence for admins: you probably cannot run your own SteamCMD or Docker server; confirm with your host. Several commercial hosting pages advertised pre-launch capacity; treat these as marketing, not evidence of an available server download.

**Admin changes confirmed in 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026)** [5][6][7]:

- Daily scheduled restart time, set in UTC.
- RCON AllowedHosts setting to restrict which hosts can reach RCON.
- RCON message and broadcast lengths capped; RCON responses default to Standard detail rather than Full; config responses no longer expose server internals.
- ServerImageURL is validated at config load.
- Since 0.11, community server IDs persist across map changes and restarts [3].

**Unofficial RCON and config reference** (fan site, self-described as not official docs and subject to change; player-reported) [10]:

- RCON is plain HTTP REST with JSON, base `http://<host>:<port>/v1/`, default port 7776 (`-RCONPort=`), no TLS, so the password crosses the network in clear text.
- Authentication is `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>`; one token has full read and write access; there is no read-only role. The listener is off by default (`bEnabled` in `[/Script/WDRCON.WDRCONSettings]`).
- Endpoint groups: status, players, bans, config, rotation, capabilities; writes include kick, kill, message, ban, broadcast and match map/end/restart. `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document and supports `If-Match` revision checks.
- Listed `ServerSettings.ini` keys include `ServerName`, `ServerPassword`, `ServerImageURL` (1024x256), cash and level min/max limits, `MaxReservedSlots` (default 20), `MaxPlayers` (listed default 128), `MinimumRequiredPlayers` (default 60), KOTH `ScorePeriod` (default 24 s) and map rotation (`Ordered` or `Random`).
- Several endpoints were reported removed in build ++Wardogs+Live-CL-501228 (2026-09-14) in favour of the config document [10].
- Assessment: because RCON uses one shared secret over unencrypted HTTP, restrict AllowedHosts and keep it on a private network or behind a TLS proxy. Confidence Medium, resting on [6] and [10].

**Third-party tools** (player-reported, not endorsed): Warcon, an open-source (MIT) self-hostable multi-server RCON panel with per-admin roles and audit log [13]; BattleMetrics has reportedly added WARDOGS RCON support [11]. The guide at [11] was written by Warcon's builders, so its recommendations are promotional.

**Hosting provider material** (secondary): BisectHosting summarises the 0.1.2 admin changes [5]; its support article on changing the automatic restart time returned HTTP 403 and is not cited. Host guides disagree on any built-in restart timer value (12 h versus 24 h of uptime); unverified.

**Modding.** The Steam page lists no mod support [1]. No official modding toolkit or plan was found.

**Client notes.** Kernel-level anti-cheat is listed [1]; Linux is unsupported [8]; Windows 11 update KB5124010 caused crash WD-L020, fixed 30 Sep 2026 [6].

text:
WARDOGS pairs a combined-arms vehicle set (tanks, an artillery tank, helicopters, light ground vehicles) with player-built Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) and a destructible battlefield. The Steam page confirms that vehicles and logistics are part of Early Access, that players can build a forward operating base to fortify a chokepoint, that rocket launchers can take down apartment blocks, and that fighter jets are planned only for the full release [1].

Official sources give no vehicle table. Names, prices and unlock levels here come from the Season 1 launch changelog as reproduced by press [2] and from community guides, which are labelled player-reported and disagree in places. Build and logistics mechanics (hammer tiers, supply types, pallets) are likewise guide-sourced [5][6][7]. Update 0.1.2 changes to rewards for destroying buildables and delivering pallets are confirmed by two press summaries [3][4].

Document confidence is Medium: the headline mechanics are official, but nearly every number rests on press reproductions or player reports, and Early Access churns per patch.

text:
- Early Access includes vehicles and logistics; fighter jets are planned for the full release only (Steam page, 2026-10-08) [1].
- Players can build their own FOB; the Season 1 changelog raised the vendor FOB price from $2,500 to $7,500 (10 Sep 2026) [1][2].
- Vehicles are bought per life from a Vehicle Vendor in the safe zone, with higher tiers needing a one-time unlock fee and a track level (player-reported, 2026-10-08) [5][8].
- Unlock tracks are Driver (ground), Pilot (helicopters) and Career/Wardog (heavy armour, artillery); Artillery moved to Career level 90 and Heavy Tank to Driver level 35 in Season 1 [2][8].
- A FOB is not a respawn point; forward spawns come from a team armoured spawn vehicle unlocked at 20 team points (player-reported) [6][7].
- Update 0.1.2 capped vehicle fly-through rewards, reduced rewards for pallets deposited outside a FOB zone, and scaled rewards for destroying buildables by build progress [3][4].
- Anything built can be destroyed; hammers also dismantle and repair (player-reported) [7].

## Vehicle roster

No official roster was retrievable. The table merges the Season 1 changelog [2] with two community guides [5][8], which are player-reported and partly conflict. Prices are per-spawn costs; "unlock" is a one-time fee.

| Class | Vehicle | Spawn price (player-reported) | Unlock gate |
|-------|---------|-------------------------------|-------------|
| Ground | Bobcat (quad) | about $500 [5] | none [5][8] |
| Ground | Dune Buggy | unlock price now $25,000 [2] | level 8 [2] |
| Ground | Kodiak (pickup) | $3,000 [8]; $2,500 [5] | Driver 10, $35,000 unlock [8] |
| Ground | Kodiak M249 / Assault | $3,750 [5][8] | level 6 [2]; Driver 6, $50,000 [8] |
| Ground | Humvee (base / M249 / minigun) | $3,000 / $3,750 / $4,500 [5] | minigun level 30 [2]; Driver 15 / 20 / 30 [8] |
| Ground | URAL / Ural Defender (M249) | $6,000 / $6,750 [8] | URAL level 3, $35,000 [2]; Defender Driver 18, M249 Driver 25 [8] |
| Ground | Heavy tank | about $14,000 (L2A6, unconfirmed) [5] | Driver 35 [2] |
| Ground | Flakpanzer Gepard (anti-air) | $10,000 [8]; about $8,000 [5] | Wardog track [8] |
| Ground | SPH-2 artillery tank | about $8,000 spawn [5] | $500,000, Career level 90 [2] |
| Air | AH-6M (miniguns) | $7,000 [8] | Pilot 4, $50,000 [8] |
| Air | AH-6R (rockets) | $12,500 [8] | Pilot 20, $250,000 [8] |
| Air | Z20 Lakota | $7,400 [5]; $8,000 with miniguns [8] | Pilot 10 [5]; Pilot 25 [8]; $35,000 [2] |
| Air | Havoc | about $18,000 [5] | Pilot 35 [5] |

Season 1 also gave the Z20 Lakota a balance pass and pitch fix, capped vehicle turret operator rotation speed, and applied helicopter input damping to all input devices [2]. No naval vehicles appear in any source retrieved. One guide counts roughly 20 vehicles and names about 16 [5].

## Purchasing and delivery

Player-reported flow [5][8]:

1. Stand at the Vehicle Vendor stall in the safe zone and choose a vehicle in the LAND or AIR tab.
2. Pay the one-time unlock fee if the vehicle is gated, then the spawn price, which is charged every purchase with no confirmation prompt [8].
3. The vehicle appears for the buyer; armed variants cost more and die to the same anti-vehicle weapons [5].

Free options reported: a team armoured spawn vehicle unlocked at 20 team points, with a satellite dish that disables it if destroyed and about a ten-minute per-player cooldown, plus free transport helicopters and SUVs a few minutes into a match [8]. Cargo vehicles carry small supply amounts; larger loads move on pallets bought at the Garage Vendor [7]. One guide claims helicopters can carry the crate or pallet loads; external sling-loading was not confirmed.

## FOB construction

Player-reported costs and rules [6][7]:

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| FOB kit | $7,500, no unlock (Season 1) [2][6]; an older guide says about $2,500 [7] |
| Small Hammer | default, $100 [6][7] |
| Medium Hammer | Support level 3 [6][7]; unlock $25,000 [6] |
| Large Hammer | Support level 8, $75,000 unlock [6]; one guide says level 7 [7] |
| Build Supplies | $10 each or $500 for a 50 stack [6] |

Procedure: deploy the kit on valid ground (not inside a building, a main base or another FOB's radius), deposit supplies into base storage via the FOB console, pick a structure from the build wheel, and hit the yellow X markers to finish [6]. Small Hammer structures (sandbags, barbed wire, hedgehogs, Recon Tent) need no FOB; HESCO, doors and gates need Medium; bunkers, Recon Towers, mortars, anti-air, Repair and Refuel Stations and the Drill Rig need Large [6]. The required tier applies only to starting a blueprint; any hammer finishes it [6]. Reported build costs include Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901 and Drill Rig 1,351 supplies [7].

Supply types: Build, Ammo (mortar, CIWS, SAM), Fuel (Refuel Station, Drill Rig) and Mechanical (Repair Station) [6]. FOBs do not refill by themselves [7]. The Drill Rig is reported to pull the Hot Zone toward the FOB when fuelled [9]. Gates admit vehicles, doors are infantry-only and hedgehogs block vehicle routes [7]. Repair Stations repair and Refuel Stations refuel vehicles from stored supplies [7].

## Destruction

The store page states rocket launchers can take down apartment blocks and tanks can tear through towns [1]. Guides report that anything built can be destroyed, with artillery used to level fortifications from outside the zone [7]. Hammers switch to "Dismantle" on finished objects and also repair [7]. Pallets left outside storage can be destroyed, and enemies reaching the FOB console can hack and take control of the base, with a siren (player-reported) [6]. Vehicles: a destroyed vehicle is gone and must be re-bought; a damaged one can be repaired at a Repair Station using Mechanical Supplies; a rolled vehicle can be flipped and repaired in the base repair area (player-reported) [5][8]. No source gives structure health values.
